body.statement:
Restrict attention to legal triangular arrays for which
\[
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{K_N}{N^{q_d}}=0,
\]
equivalently, arrays that are not eventually bounded below by any positive constant multiple of \(N^{q_d}\). Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\), determine explicit rate functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) such that
\[
R_d(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K),
\qquad
E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)
\]
along every such array, including the exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition. The answer must be subsequence-stable: for every subsequence \(\mathcal S\) on which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) remains arbitrarily small, meaning
\[
\liminf_{N\to\infty,\,N\in\mathcal S}\frac{K_N}{N^{q_d}}=0,
\]
it must establish the asserted rates on every further subsequence \(\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal S\) for which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), and it must combine those rates with the established root-\(N\) bounds on further subsequences where \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) is bounded below by a positive constant. Thus an array that oscillates between small- and large-arm regimes may not be discarded. The lower-bound branch must instantiate the finite-support simultaneous family so that \(\Delta_{N,K}\) matches the claimed rate, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}>0\), thereby giving nonnegative reduced cost against every rematching column and strict slack off the declared contact columns; its ordered low-versus-high version must also prove the one-sided expected-excess-length converse. The upper-bound branch must construct a computable estimator and a uniformly honest lower confidence bound with numerically specified calibration attaining the respective rates, or prove a sharper shared-geometric dual bound and supply the calibration needed for honesty. The existence of the unspecified constant \(C_d\) in \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) alone does not make that theoretical rule numerically computable.
body.justification: After removing every subsequence whose arm ratio is bounded below, the remaining task is the exact estimation and ordered one-sided frontier on all small-ratio subsequences, assembled coherently across irregular arrays.
body.gap: Exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms, the missing arm factor, every-rematching strict off-contact certificate, numerical honest calibration, and the ordered one-sided converse remain unresolved.
body.consumer: A solution would complete the decision-theoretic account for every legal array with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\) and splice it with the established root-\(N\) regimes.

obligation.what_is_open: Determine matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided lower bounds, or a sharper matching computable upper procedure, on every subsequence with \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), including exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition; then assemble these with the established root-\(N\) subsequences to cover every irregular legal array with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\).
obligation.obstruction: The available nonparametric converse is the embedded two-margin order \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), whereas the proved plug-in upper contribution is \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). No instantiated simultaneous-marginal family currently preserves a separation of the missing order against every rematching column while keeping mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and no sharper aggregate theorem for all jointly conjugate dual potentials is available. The theoretical plug-in confidence rule also contains an unspecified existence constant and therefore is not by itself a numerically calibrated solution.
obligation.attempted: The residual envelope, arbitrary-subset support exchange, optimal-sum diameter, common-support empirical interpolation, two-margin reduction, ordered Bernoulli pair, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) theorems, rational empirical-MOT certificate, sparse-arm gadgets, parity witnesses, and fixed-dimensional orthogonal constructions have been checked. The latter constructions do not close the arm factor because alternative margins can rematch, and neither the finite-family branch nor the aggregate-dual branch has supplied the missing certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
Under balanced armwise product sampling, unit-ball support, fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), and \(m=N/K\ge2\), the established finite-sample bounds are
\[
c_d\max\left\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\right\}
\le R_d(N,K)
\le C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right]
\]
and
\[
c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}
\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
Here \(r=\min\{K,d\}\), and the upper expected-length bound is attained by the theoretical rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) after choosing a finite constant \(C_d\) whose existence is proved by the plug-in upper theorem. This proves uniform root-\(N\) order for both risks whenever \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with
\[
q_5=\frac16,
\qquad
q_d=\frac14\quad\text{for }d\ge6.
\]
Independently, the mean-floor rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is numerically explicit, requires no multi-marginal transport computation, is uniformly honest, and has worst-case expected excess length of order \(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2\); hence it yields a no-MOT root-\(N\) baseline when \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). For rational empirical input, \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\) computes primal and dual certificates bracketing \(L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\) to any rational width \(\epsilon\), in fixed-dimensional time polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\). What remains unresolved is a matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided converse, or a sharper matching upper bound, on every subsequence along which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), including fixed-\(K\) logarithms and all intervening transitions.
